narrative: Material PL1__MA3669E0 exhibits near-continuous demand averaging 457 units/day with moderate variability (CV=0.33) and no detectable trend over the observation period. Lead times average 4.03 days with moderate stability (CV=0.397) after removing two erroneous observations exceeding 9,000 days. The optimized (r,Q) policy establishes a safety stock of 1,303 units to achieve 95% service level, with order quantity capped at 2,700 units due to the 4,004-unit storage constraint — reducing annual total costs by 26.4% versus the current SAP baseline.
warnings: EOQ constrained from 7196 to 2700 units due to max_storage_units=4003.895
Post-replenishment stock reaches ~100% of storage capacity (4003/4004 units)
2 extreme lead time outliers removed (9201.55 and 9327.37 days) as data errors
SAP safety stock is 0 — current policy provides no buffer against demand/lead time uncertainty

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (100% non-zero working days) with moderate and stationary variability, making a continuous-review (r,Q) policy optimal. The fixed MOQ of 1,636 units is naturally incorporated as a lower bound on Q. An (s,S) policy offers no advantage given the absence of lumpy or intermittent demand patterns.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint: the unconstrained EOQ of 7,196 units cannot be satisfied within the 4,004-unit storage limit. The capped order quantity of 2,700 units increases ordering frequency and raises annual ordering costs above the unconstrained optimum. Expanding storage by ~3,200 units would allow full EOQ exploitation and further reduce total annual costs.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1,636) + safety_stock (1,303) = 2,939 units, which is within max_storage_units (4,004). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
